title: EU-CELAC 2021-2023 Strategic Roadmap for Science, Technology, and Innovation Cooperation
executive_summary: The EU-CELAC 2021-2023 Strategic Roadmap outlines joint priorities for research and innovation between the European Union and the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC). Building on the Brussels Declaration and Action Plan, the roadmap focuses on four pillars: researcher mobility, research infrastructures, global challenges (health, environment, digital), and innovation. Key actions include enhancing academic mobility, strengthening research infrastructure collaboration, addressing shared global challenges such as COVID-19, climate change, and digital transformation, and integrating innovation as a core area of cooperation. The roadmap emphasizes open science, data sharing, and the use of EU programs like Horizon Europe to deepen bi-regional collaboration. It calls for systemic, multidisciplinary approaches and highlights the importance of policy exchange, capacity building, and inclusive, sustainable development. Progress will be reviewed at future Senior Officials Meetings.
characteristics: Four Pillars: The roadmap is structured around four pillars—Research Infrastructures, Researcher Mobility, Global Challenges (health, environment, digital), and Innovation—aimed at deepening EU-CELAC cooperation in science, technology, and innovation.

Strategic Priorities: Focus areas include health (pandemics, chronic diseases), environmental sustainability (climate change, biodiversity, sustainable agriculture, Atlantic Ocean research), digital transformation (connectivity, cybersecurity, digital skills), and fostering innovation ecosystems.

Researcher Mobility & Capacity Building: Emphasizes academic and researcher mobility, capacity building, and support for doctoral/postdoctoral programs, with tools like Erasmus+, Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and the Euraxess portal.

Open Science & Data Sharing: Strong commitment to open access publishing, responsible research data management (FAIR principles), and exploring joint initiatives for open science and data commons between the regions.

Innovation Ecosystem: Recognizes innovation as a key pillar, promoting collaboration between academia and business, support for intellectual property, technology transfer, smart specialization, and social innovation.

Policy Alignment & Programmes: Encourages use of EU programmes like Horizon Europe, supports policy dialogue, and calls for working groups to align activities with these strategic priorities and report progress regularly.

Political Actors: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
Research and Innovation Actors: Latin American Cooperation of Advanced Networks

practical_applications: The EU-CELAC Working Group (WG) on Research Infrastructures, established in 2017, is actively working on roadmapping, governance, access policies, and practical support for partnering of research infrastructures between the EU and CELAC regions.

The EU-LAC RESInfra project, funded by the EU Framework Programme for Research and Innovation (Horizon 2020), is supporting the operation of the Research Infrastructures Working Group and facilitating closer collaboration between EU and CELAC research infrastructures.
The extension of the Euraxess mobility portal to the entire CELAC region is being implemented to support researcher mobility and knowledge transfer.

Ongoing support and promotion of Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions under Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ for human capital development, international collaboration, and knowledge transfer between the EU and CELAC.
The CELAC Network of Specialists in Infectious Agents and Emerging and Re-emerging Diseases is an active regional research network supported by the partnership.

Participation and cooperation in existing global health research initiatives, such as the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD), Global Research Collaboration for Infectious Diseases Prevention (GloPID-R), Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), and GAVI ('the Vaccine Alliance'), are being promoted and supported.
The European COVID-19 Data Platform (www.covid19dataportal.org) is being used to coordinate open science and data sharing between the EU and CELAC regions.
The BELLA cable project is being implemented to establish a high-speed digital link between the EU and CELAC regions, with ongoing efforts to extend its reach within CELAC countries.

EU pilot actions on smart specialisation are being conducted in the Latin America and Caribbean region, supported under the EU Regional Facility for Development in Transition, to test and promote innovation-driven sustainable territorial development.
The Horizon Europe programme, launched in 2021, is open to CELAC participation, with specific calls and partnerships flagged to boost EU-CELAC cooperation in research and innovation.

Ongoing support for open access publishing and research data management initiatives in CELAC states, including the implementation of data repositories in higher education institutions and research organisations.

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants highlighted the importance of developing common approaches to the complex challenges which most urgently face both continents. They highlighted the essential contribution of social sciences and the humanities to address the global challenges and recognised that engineering sciences and mathematics are transversal disciplines at the interface of science, technology and the needs of society.
kpi_list.metric_name: Development of Common Approaches to Global Challenges
kpi_list.target_description: Develop common approaches to address urgent global challenges, integrating social sciences, humanities, engineering, and mathematics
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of established joint approaches and integration of disciplines in initiatives
kpi_list.responsible_entity: EU-CELAC Joint Initiative on Research and Innovation (JIRI) Participants

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants pointed to the vital role of academic and researcher mobility as the basis of knowledge transfer and intercultural understanding between the regions, and of developing stronger links between research infrastructures as a platform for common scientific and innovation endeavours and the sharing of improved data, particularly in the areas of the global challenges.
kpi_list.target_description: Strengthen academic and researcher mobility and links between research infrastructures for knowledge transfer and data sharing
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking mobility programs, partnerships, and data sharing initiatives

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants highlighted the importance of reinforcing the tools and instruments to inform on existing national, regional and Union programmes supporting human capital development, international collaboration and knowledge transfer, such as the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions under Horizon Europe and Erasmus+. The Participants also welcomed the extension of the Euraxess mobility portal to the whole CELAC region.
kpi_list.target_description: Extend the Euraxess mobility portal to the entire CELAC region
kpi_list.measurement_method: Confirmation of portal accessibility and usage statistics in CELAC countries
kpi_list.responsible_entity: EU-CELAC JIRI Working Group on Researcher Mobility

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants encouraged a full exploitation of the results of projects thematically close to the Coronavirus disease that have been launched in the previous years, for a further boost to the current global efforts to tackle the pandemic and for efficient building of resilience and preparedness.
kpi_list.metric_name: Exploitation of COVID-19 Related Research Results
kpi_list.target_description: Fully exploit results of previous COVID-19 related projects to boost pandemic response and resilience
kpi_list.measurement_method: Review of project outcomes and integration into policy and practice

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants emphasised the essential role that joint research, demonstration and deployment of innovative means and methods have in reducing this risk and drew the attention to the potential of using data and related services (e.g. remote sensing, community data, Copernicus service) to provide additional assistance to this effort.
kpi_list.metric_name: Joint Research and Innovation for Wildfire Risk Reduction
kpi_list.target_description: Conduct joint research, demonstration, and deployment of innovative methods to reduce wildfire risk using data services
kpi_list.measurement_method: Number and impact of joint research projects and data-driven initiatives

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants highlighted the necessity for a systemic approach to the challenges and opportunities offered by the Atlantic Ocean, including its subsets such as the Caribbean, and welcomed the move towards an All-Atlantic Ocean Research Alliance, where active involvement of CELAC countries could bring further benefits, through enhanced cooperation of countries connected to the Atlantic Ocean, including through instrument such as the Atlantic International Research Centre (AIR Centre). Special attention should be given to youth involvement (ocean literacy and beyond).
kpi_list.metric_name: Establishment of All-Atlantic Ocean Research Alliance with CELAC Involvement
kpi_list.target_description: Establish and enhance the All-Atlantic Ocean Research Alliance with active CELAC participation and youth involvement
kpi_list.measurement_method: Alliance formation, participation records, and youth engagement activities

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants highlighted the value of the BELLA cable to further boost the future cooperation potential in all areas, including research and innovation, and continue to explore the extension of the cable to maximise its reach within the CELAC countries.
kpi_list.target_description: Explore and implement the extension of the BELLA cable to maximize connectivity within CELAC countries
kpi_list.measurement_method: Progress reports on cable extension and connectivity coverage

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants encouraged a joint work between EU and CELAC in defining common standards and promoting their adoption at the global level.
kpi_list.metric_name: Definition and Promotion of Common Digital Standards
kpi_list.target_description: Define and promote adoption of common digital standards between EU and CELAC at the global level
kpi_list.measurement_method: Documentation of standardization initiatives and adoption rates

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants underlined the need to continue developing the digital skills necessary for the citizens and economy to thrive in this period of digital transition. Special attention should be given to areas of particular significance to the society, such as big data or artificial intelligence.
kpi_list.metric_name: Development of Digital Skills in Key Areas
kpi_list.target_description: Develop digital skills for citizens and the economy, with focus on big data and artificial intelligence
kpi_list.measurement_method: Implementation of training programs and assessment of skill development

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Participants underlined the importance of deepening the work on the EU-CELAC Common Research Area, in particular by adding 'Innovation' as its fourth fundamental pillar. Innovation should thus become one of the key areas of policy collaboration between the two regions.
kpi_list.metric_name: Integration of Innovation as Fourth Pillar in EU-CELAC Common Research Area
kpi_list.target_description: Integrate 'Innovation' as a fundamental pillar in the EU-CELAC Common Research Area and make it a key area of policy collaboration
kpi_list.measurement_method: Official adoption and implementation of innovation pillar in policy documents

sdg_alignment: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is a principal actor throughout the document, co-leading the EU-CELAC partnership, shaping the strategic roadmap, and providing key funding and policy frameworks (e.g., Horizon Europe). The EU is central to all main topics, decisions, and initiatives discussed, including research, innovation, and open science.

top_actors.name: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
top_actors.justification: CELAC is the EU's counterpart in the bi-regional partnership, co-endorsing the roadmap, participating in all key decisions, and representing the Latin American and Caribbean region in the joint initiatives. CELAC's involvement is essential for the implementation and success of the strategic roadmap.

top_actors.name: European Commission
top_actors.justification: The European Commission is repeatedly referenced as the executive body responsible for implementing the EU's side of the roadmap, hosting meetings, and managing key programmes (e.g., Horizon Europe). It plays a leading role in operationalizing the partnership and facilitating cooperation.

top_themes.name: Bi-regional Cooperation
top_themes.justification: The central focus of the document is the strategic roadmap for cooperation between the EU and CELAC regions in research and innovation. Bi-regional cooperation is the overarching theme, explicitly referenced throughout the text as the foundation for all other initiatives, pillars, and objectives. The document's main message is to strengthen and operationalize this cooperation, making it the most central and strategically important theme.

top_themes.name: Innovation
top_themes.justification: Innovation is elevated as a new, fourth pillar in the EU-CELAC Common Research Area, marking a significant strategic shift. The document dedicates substantial content to the importance of innovation for sustainable and inclusive development, the need for systemic approaches, and the creation of innovation ecosystems. It is directly tied to key objectives and commitments, such as economic growth, technological advancement, and policy collaboration.

top_themes.name: Global Challenges (Health, Environment, Digital Transformation)
top_themes.justification: Addressing global challenges—specifically health (including COVID-19), environmental sustainability (green transition), and digital transformation—is a core pillar of the roadmap. The document devotes extensive sections to these topics, outlining joint actions, priorities, and the need for coordinated responses. These challenges are strategically important as they represent shared priorities and urgent needs for both regions, directly relating to the roadmap's objectives.
